title: What number appears after ten presses of plus ten lakh?
description: The biggest button of Creative Chitti adds ten lakh. The video presses it ten times, finds the number, counts its zeros and learns its name. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that ten times ten lakh is ten lakh lakh.
teaching_notes: One idea: ten presses of ten lakh make one hundred lakhs, and one hundred lakhs is called one crore, a one followed by seven zeros. Ask the class to count only the lakhs before writing the number. Watch for students who multiply the unit name as well as the counts.

source: What if we press the +10,00,000 button ten times? What number will come up? How many zeroes will it have? What should we call it?
video_script.why: The child knows a lakh has five zeros and can multiply ten by ten.
video_script.substitution: Ten presses of ten lakh make one hundred lakhs, which is called one crore and is a one followed by seven zeros.
video_script.anchor: Press the plus ten lakh button ten times: what number appears, how many zeros has it, and what is it called?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the unit name as well as the counts, and calls ten times ten lakh ten lakh lakh. Lakh is a unit that stays as it is; ten times ten is one hundred, so it is one hundred lakh.
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred lakhs make one crore, a one followed by seven zeros

final_answer.value: 1,00,00,000, which is 100 lakhs, 1 followed by seven zeros, called a crore

maths_rules: 100 lakhs = 100 × 1,00,000: a lakh has 5 zeros and × 100 adds 2 more, so 7 zeros
100 lakhs = 1,00,00,000 = 1 crore, a one followed by seven zeros
the slip: ten lakh lakh multiplies the unit name
video_script.design: One idea: count the lakhs, ten times ten is one hundred, and one hundred lakhs is one crore. Wrong idea: Keeko multiplies the unit name. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
